decided: Jeremy, 2026-11-10 (240 Hz stimulus rendering on omnifin0; the render rate joins the protocol identity in the shape Palette proposed: a new recipe, a session-level exact integer, always present)
supersedes: semantic_policy_pairing_v2.json (revision 2). That file is unchanged and stays pinned by the admissions that already pin it.
hash_rule: protocol_semantic_hash = 'sha256:' + hex(sha256(canonical_json_bytes)) over the exact recorded bytes; a consumer never re-canonicalises or regenerates them

pairings.trial_index: schema_version 3 (citrus.protocol.trial_index.v3) for all three semantic policies

mixing: any other combination is corruption and is refused; semantic.v3 or semantic.v4 under the legacy convention is refused; an unknown policy (for example citrus.protocol.semantic.v5) is refused

semantic_v4.changes_from_v3: normalization_policy is citrus.protocol.semantic.v4, and the identity gains one session-level key. Everything else in the envelope and identity is hashed exactly as in v3.

newly_hashed.rule: required on every v4 identity, 120 included; a JSON integer (no fraction, no scale object), positive. It is the process's stimulus frame rate: arena update ticks and display submissions per second. Citrus refuses to build a v4 identity for a rate that is not a whole number of hertz (status code stimulus_render_rate_invalid), so a recording at such a rate has no semantic hash.
newly_hashed.allowed_values: 120 or 240 as of 2026-11-10; Citrus refuses to launch at any other rate

semantic_v4.consistency: in a v4 recording, identity.stimulus_render_rate_hz equals the H5's display_submission_rate_target_hz and stimulus_frame_rate_nominal_hz. All three come from one per-process value in Citrus (StimulusTiming::FrameRateHz), set once at launch. Palette refuses a recording where they differ.
semantic_v4.why: the chaser draws random numbers once per update tick, and other per-tick behaviour may differ, so the same protocol and seed show a different stimulus at 240 Hz than at 120 Hz; one hash must never name both
semantic_v4.trial_index: stays schema_version 3 / citrus.protocol.trial_index.v3, with no new keys; its bytes differ from a v3-era trial index only in the embedded protocol_semantic_hash value, as for semantic v2 to v3. Its hash changes because it embeds the semantic hash, and the execution-index hash changes because it embeds the trial-index hash.
semantic_v4.seeds: per_session_v1 chaser seeds are sha256('citrus.chaser_schedule.seed.v1' | session_uuid | semantic_hash | step_index | occurrence), so they change with the semantic hash; session_uuid is included, so no two sessions ever shared a seed and a v4 session at 120 Hz is a replicate of a v3 session in the same sense as two v3 sessions. fixed_v1 seeds are unchanged, but at 240 Hz the trajectory they produce differs from 120 Hz because draws happen per tick.
semantic_v4.rate_history: Citrus rendered at a compile-time 120 Hz until main 7e92836 (2026-11-10), and 7e92836 allows only 120. Every v1, v2 and v3 recording therefore ran at 120 Hz.

relabel_pooling_rule.scope: protocol_semantic_hash grouping only; trial-index and execution-index hashes are never joined across policies
relabel_pooling_rule.rule_v3_to_v4: a v3 recording joins a v4 protocol group only if (1) its recorded protocol_semantic_json bytes hash to its recorded v3 protocol_semantic_hash, (2) the byte substring },"normalization_policy":"citrus.protocol.semantic.v3" occurs exactly once in those bytes, and (3) sha256 of the bytes with that substring replaced by ,"stimulus_render_rate_hz":120},"normalization_policy":"citrus.protocol.semantic.v4" equals the v4 group's protocol_semantic_hash. Otherwise the recording stays in its own v3 group.
relabel_pooling_rule.why_the_substring_works: the canonical JSON is minified with keys in sorted order, so the identity object is the first key and closes immediately before ,"normalization_policy"; within identity, stimulus_render_rate_hz sorts after steps and is therefore its last key
relabel_pooling_rule.rate: only 120 is ever inserted, because every v3 recording ran at 120 Hz (rate_history); a v3 recording never joins a v4 group at 240
relabel_pooling_rule.chaining: a v2 recording reaches v4 only by applying the revision-2 v2-to-v3 rule and then this rule, each step on bytes, each step checked
relabel_pooling_rule.inputs: recorded bytes only; never a re-serialisation or a fresh regeneration
relabel_pooling_rule.expected: matches every v3 protocol at 120 Hz; never matches a v4 identity at 240 Hz

fixture.source: Citrus protocol_identity_dump --render-rate-hz 120 and 240, built from the producer branch; v3 bytes from main 7e92836
fixture.status: generated 2026-11-10 from the producer branch; five repository protocols, each at v3 (main 7e92836), v4 at 120 and v4 at 240; the v3-to-v4 relabel rule matches all five at 120 and none at 240
